assumptions.condition: For fixed \(0<\gamma_-\le\gamma_+<\infty\), every nonzero singular value of \(\mathcal C_D\) lies in \([\gamma_-,\gamma_+]\) when \(d>0\).
For fixed \(0<\kappa_-\le\kappa_+<\infty\), every eigenvalue of \(\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)b_0(t)^\top\,dt\) lies in \([\kappa_-,\kappa_+]\) when \(d>0\).

For \(d=r-1\) and \(d\ge1\), let \(z_m^{(N,d)}\) be obtained, for each \(N\ge2d+1\), by empirical Gram--Schmidt from the explicitly centered columns
\[
 q_{k,m}^{(N)}=\{m-(N+1)/2\}^k-N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N}\{\ell-(N+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le k\le d,
\]
and define \(R_d=\sup_{N\ge2d+1}\max_{1\le m\le N}\|z_m^{(N,d)}\|_2\), with \(R_0=0\), let \(\Phi_d\) be the deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\)-orthonormalization of \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), with first coordinate \(\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), and put \(A_{p,d}=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d\), and suppose the fixed primitive constants obey
\[
 g_-\le1,
 \qquad
 R_d\le M_z,
 \qquad
 \gamma_-^2\le(a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2)\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\gamma_+^2,
 \qquad
 \kappa_-\le a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2\le\kappa_+,
\]
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}\|A_{p,d}(t)\|_2\le M_b,
 \qquad
 2|a_{\circ,0}|h_\circ c_f^{-1/2}
 \left\{\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \le\frac34(1/2-\alpha),
\]
and, writing \(v_\circ=|a_{\circ,1}|/4\), for every \(p\in\{0,1\}\), every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(\|x\|_2\le R_d\), every \(|v|\le v_\circ\), and every \(t\in\mathcal I\), the curve
\[
 \ell_{p,x,v}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}+A_{p,d}(t)^\top x+\mathbf 1\{p=1\}v\psi_\circ(t)
\]
satisfies
\[
 s_-\le\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\le1,
 \qquad
 -\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{t\in\operatorname{supp}(\psi_\circ')}[-\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}(t)]\ge c_f,
 \qquad
 \left\|-\frac{\partial_t\ell_{p,x,v}}{\ell_{p,x,v}}\right\|_{C^\beta(\mathcal I)}\le L;
\]
and for \(d=0\), the same four inequalities hold with the empty factor term, \(x=0\), and every \(|v|\le v_\circ\).

definitions.name: Canonical normalized survival-factor coordinates
definitions.construction:
Set
\[
 s_p(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t).
\]
Start from the model's target-compatible all-unit affine representation, center its donor loadings, covariance-normalize those loadings, and apply the inverse normalization to the factor curves. Write the singular-value decomposition of the resulting primitive centered operator as
\[
 \mathcal C_D=\sum_{k=1}^d\sigma_k u_k\otimes v_k,
\]
ordered by decreasing \(\sigma_k\) with deterministic sign and tie-breaking rules, and define
\[
 z_{m,k}=\sqrt{N_0}v_{k,m},
 \qquad b_{p,k}(t)=\sigma_k u_{k,p}(t).
\]
Thus the construction uses the donor-centered normalization
\[
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m=0,
 \qquad N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d.
\]
Let
\[
 H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)b_0(t)^\top\,dt.
\]
Conditional on the model's target-pre factor compatibility
\(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0\in\operatorname{span}\{b_{0,1},\ldots,b_{0,d}\}\), define the shared target coordinate by
\[
 z_\star=H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)
 \{S^0_{0,\star}(t)-s_0(t)\}\,dt.
\]
The positive canonical pre-period Gram makes this coordinate unique. Transporting the compatible all-unit representation through the same covariance normalization and orthogonal donor-SVD transform gives
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m
\]
for both periods and every donor or target unit. Survival normalization gives \(s_p(0)=1\) and \(b_p(0)=0\). When \(d=0\), compatibility forces every contrast to vanish and all vectors, sums, and Gram matrices use the zero-dimensional convention.

definitions.name: Exact-rank censored Synthetic Survival Control class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)=\{P_{N_0,K_T,K_D}: P_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:control-consistency},\mathrm{ass:patient-independence},\mathrm{ass:independent-censoring},\mathrm{ass:censor-overlap},\mathrm{ass:event-overlap},\mathrm{ass:hazard-smoothness},\mathrm{ass:normalized-factor-model},\mathrm{ass:exact-centered-rank},\mathrm{ass:centered-contrast-spectrum},\mathrm{ass:pre-contrast-gram},\mathrm{ass:donor-incoherence},\mathrm{ass:target-loading-bound},\mathrm{ass:factor-envelope}\}\). Exact rank is imposed on the primitive operator \(\mathcal C_D\); for \(r=1\), its rank is zero and every contrast-space object uses the zero-dimensional convention.

definitions.name: Per-triple uniform continuous-time honesty class
definitions.construction: For each evaluated triple, define \(\mathcal H_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)=\{B:\inf_{P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)}P\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\le\theta(t)\le B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\}\ge1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)\}\). Thus admissibility is enforced at the same triple at which width is evaluated, while \(\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)\) vanishes uniformly on every three-dimensional tail.

definitions.name: Explicit normalization-preserving fixed-rank target-loading pairs
definitions.construction:
Fix \(d=r-1\).  For every integer \(N_0\ge2d+1\) and \(1\le k\le d\), define the explicitly centered donor column
\[
 q_{k,m}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}^k-
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{N_0}\{\ell-(N_0+1)/2\}^k,
 \qquad 1\le m\le N_0.
\]
Apply deterministic empirical Gram--Schmidt to \(q_1,\ldots,q_d\) in the inner product \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m xy\), orienting each column to have positive leading polynomial coefficient, and denote the resulting row vectors by \(z_m^{(N_0,d)}\).  Thus every column is mean zero and \(N_0^{-1}\sum_m z_m^{(N_0,d)}z_m^{(N_0,d)\top}=I_d\); for \(d=1\), \(z_{m,1}^{(N_0,1)}=\{m-(N_0+1)/2\}/\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}\).

For \(d\ge1\), apply deterministic \(L^2(\mathcal I)\) Gram--Schmidt to \(\psi_\circ,t\psi_\circ,\ldots,t^{d-1}\psi_\circ\), orient the first function as \(\varphi_{1,d}=\psi_\circ/\|\psi_\circ\|_2\), write \(\Phi_d=(\varphi_{1,d},\ldots,\varphi_{d,d})^\top\), and set
\[
 A_{p,d}(t)=a_{\circ,p}\|\psi_\circ\|_2\Phi_d(t).
\]
For \(u\in\{-1,+1\}\), take \(s_p(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t}\), \(b_p=A_{p,d}\), donor loadings \(z_m=z_m^{(N_0,d)}\), and target loading \(z_\star^{(u)}=u h_\circ K_T^{-1/2}e_1\).  Put
\[
 S_{p,m}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 S_{p,\star}^{(r,u)}(t)=s_p(t)+A_{p,d}(t)^\top z_\star^{(u)}
\]
on \(\mathcal I\), continue every curve after \(\bar\tau\) by its value at \(\bar\tau\) times \(e^{-\lambda_\circ(t-\bar\tau)}\), take \(C_{p,m,j}=\infty\), and let \(P_{r,u}\) be the induced independent observed-data law.  For \(r=2\), define \(P_u=P_{2,u}\).  When \(d=0\), all score arrays and factor terms are empty and the same prescription defines the homogeneous backbone.  This construction only names the laws; centering, empirical Gram, class membership, rank, spectrum, separation, and divergence are properties to be proved.

definitions.name: Rate-matched interpolation grid
definitions.construction:
Put \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\) and
\[
 J_r=\max\left\{1,
 \left\lceil\bar\tau\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)^{-1/q}\right\rceil
 \right\}.
\]
Define the canonical quasi-uniform grid and its adjacent-knot mesh by
\[
 \mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}
 =\left\{\frac{\ell\bar\tau}{J_r}:0\le\ell\le J_r\right\},
 \qquad h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=\frac{\bar\tau}{J_r}.
\]
Use piecewise-linear interpolation between adjacent knots. Then
\[
 h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}\le\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D),
 \qquad
 |\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}|
 \le2+\bar\tau\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)^{-1/q}.
\]

definitions.name: Censoring-aware functional-PCR martingale-multiplier band
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on the canonical grid. For the population comparison, define
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m},\qquad
 \widetilde s_p=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\widetilde S^0_{p,m},
\]
\[
 \widetilde Y_m=(\widetilde S^0_{0,m}-\widetilde s_0,
                  \widetilde S^0_{1,m}-\widetilde s_1),\qquad
 \widetilde\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \widetilde Y_m\otimes\widetilde Y_m.
\]
Apply the selected positive-square-root and pre-period least-squares prediction map below to this panel and call the result \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}\); for \(r=1\), put \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\widetilde s_1\). This is a proof comparison and does not redefine \(\theta\).

Put \(h_0=s_-g_-\). For any cell or deterministic half-fold containing \(k\) patients, set
\[
 \ell_k=\max\{1,kh_0/8\},\qquad
 Y_k^\dagger(u)=\max\{Y_k(u),\ell_k\}.
\]
Order tied observed failures lexicographically by failure time and patient index, updating the risk count after each ordered failure, and define
\[
 \widehat S_k^\dagger(t)=
 \prod_{u\le t}\left\{1-\frac{dN_k(u)}{Y_k^\dagger(u)}\right\}.
\]
Every ordered increment is zero or one, so this measurable curve lies in \([0,1]\) on every dataset. Interpolate it by \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\). For every \(r\ge2\), use these stabilized curves for the target-pre full cell, every donor full cell, and both odd--even donor half-folds. For \(r=1\), do not stabilize: pool all \(N_0K_D\) donor-post records first, form the ordinary aggregate-risk product-limit curve with its empty-risk convention, and interpolate it continuously.

For \(r\ge2\), center the two sets of stabilized half-fold donor curves across donors to obtain \(\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\) and \(\widehat Y_m^{(2)}\), and form
\[
 \widehat\Gamma=\frac{1}{2N_0}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}
 \{\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(2)}+
   \widehat Y_m^{(2)}\otimes\widehat Y_m^{(1)}\}.
\]
Select its largest \(d\) eigenvalues with deterministic lexicographic basis and sign rules, put \(\widehat\mu_k=\sqrt{\max\{\widehat\lambda_k,0\}}\), and set \(\widehat b_{p,k}=\widehat\mu_k\widehat u_{k,p}\). Let \(\widehat s_p\) be the donor average of the stabilized full-cell curves, and let \(\widehat H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0\widehat b_0^\top\). On the aggregate regular event
\[
 \widehat\lambda_d\ge\gamma_-^2/4,\qquad
 \widehat\lambda_d-\widehat\lambda_{d+1}\ge\gamma_-^2/4,
 \qquad \lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_0)\ge\kappa_-/4,
\]
define
\[
 \widehat z_\star=\widehat H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}\widehat b_0(t)
 \{\widehat S_{0,\star}^\dagger(t)-\widehat s_0(t)\}\,dt,
 \qquad
 \widehat\theta_r=\widehat s_1+\widehat b_1^\top\widehat z_\star.
\]
This is the rotation-invariant selected-projector, positive-square-root, and inverse-pre-Gram prediction map. If a fold is empty or an aggregate threshold fails, set the factor and loading estimates to zero and let \(\widehat\theta_r\) be the continuously interpolated ordinary pooled donor-post product-limit curve. Thus every branch is total, measurable, and continuous.

On the regular branch, differentiate the coordinate-free prediction map and the stabilized product-limit inputs. The observed contribution of patient \(j\) in a stabilized \(k\)-patient input uses the weight
\[
 -\widehat S_k^\dagger(t-)
 \int_0^t\{Y_k^\dagger(u)\}^{-1}\,dN_{k,j}(u).
\]
On the fallback and rank-one branches use the ordinary pooled aggregate-risk derivative. Attach independent standard Gaussian multipliers to the patient contributions and denote the resulting interpolated process by \(\widehat Z_r^\xi\). Define its conditional covariance by
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_r(g,g')
 =E_\xi\{\widehat Z_r^\xi(g)\widehat Z_r^\xi(g')\mid O\}.
\]
Put
\[
 q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}=1-\alpha+
 \min\left\{\frac\alpha2,
 \frac{\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}2\right\},
\]
and define the left-continuous generalized-inverse conditional quantile by
\[
 \widetilde c_r^\xi=
 \inf\left\{x\ge0:
 P_\xi\left(\max_{g\in\mathcal G}|\widehat Z_r^\xi(g)|\le x
 \mid O\right)\ge q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\right\}.
\]
For the explicit deterministic constants set
\[
 C_\partial=2^{12}r^2(1+\bar\tau)^2
 (1+M_b+M_z+M_\star+\gamma_+)^2
 (1+\gamma_-^{-1}+\kappa_-^{-1})^4,
\]
\[
 C_Z=2^{12}(1+L\bar\tau)^2(s_-g_-)^{-2}(1+C_\partial)^2.
\]
Put
\[
 d_r(\alpha)=\left(\frac{2C_Z}{\alpha}\right)^{1/2}\rho_r,
 \qquad c_r^\xi=\max\{\widetilde c_r^\xi,d_r(\alpha)\}.
\]
Thus \(c_r^\xi\) is a guarded multiplier critical radius; coverage is certified by the deterministic guard rather than by a multiplier-only random-quantile theorem.

Project \(\widehat\theta_r\) pointwise onto \([0,1]\), impose value one at zero, and call the result \(\widetilde\theta_r\). With \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), define
\[
 A_r=c_r^\xi+\mathbf1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D)
 +\omega_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 +c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q}.
\]
At each grid knot set
\[
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{lo}}=
 \max\{0,\widetilde\theta_r-A_r\},\qquad
 \widehat B_r^{\mathrm{up}}=
 \min\{1,\widetilde\theta_r+A_r\},
\]
interpolate both endpoints linearly between adjacent knots, and impose their common value one at zero. This defines the guarded martingale-multiplier functional-PCR band on every dataset.

definitions.name: Normalization-preserving rank-adaptation handle
definitions.construction: Use a patient-martingale estimate of the second normalized contrast singular value to test exact rank one against separated rank-two alternatives, and invert that test to switch between the rank-one and rank-two oracle multiplier bands while preserving \(S(0)=1\). The threshold and the adaptive band are to be derived from the composite testing problem rather than fixed in advance.

definitions.name: Separately normalized rank-at-most-two closure
definitions.construction:
For each sample-size triple, define
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\leq 2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)
=\left\{Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}:Q_{N_0,K_T,K_D}
\text{ has the properties below}\right\}.
\]
Every member satisfies
\(\mathrm{ass:control\mbox{-}consistency}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:patient\mbox{-}independence}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}censoring}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:censor\mbox{-}overlap}\),
\(\mathrm{ass:event\mbox{-}overlap}\), and
\(\mathrm{ass:hazard\mbox{-}smoothness}\), with the common constants appearing in
those assumptions.  Set, canonically,
\[
s_{p,Q}(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}S^0_{p,m}(t).
\]
There is a contrast indicator \(e_Q\in\{0,1\}\).  If \(e_Q=0\), then
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)
\quad\text{for all }p\in\{0,1\},\ m\in\mathcal M,\ t\in\mathcal I.
\]
If \(e_Q=1\), there are scalar continuous factor curves \(b_{p,Q}\) and scalar
loadings \(\zeta_{m,Q}\) such that
\[
S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_{p,Q}(t)+b_{p,Q}(t)\zeta_{m,Q},
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}=0,
\quad
N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\zeta_{m,Q}^2=1.
\]
The sign is selected canonically by requiring the first nonzero value in a fixed
countable dense sequence of continuous linear probes of
\((b_{0,Q},b_{1,Q})\) to be positive.  The invariant upper and loading bounds are
\[
0<\int_{\mathcal I}\{b_{0,Q}(t)^2+b_{1,Q}(t)^2\}\,dt\leq\gamma_+^2,
\qquad
0<\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}(t)^2\,dt\leq\kappa_+,
\]
\[
\max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\sup_{t\in\mathcal I}|b_{p,Q}(t)|\leq M_b,
\qquad
\max_{m\in\mathcal D}|\zeta_{m,Q}|\leq M_z,
\qquad
|\zeta_{\star,Q}|\leq M_\star.
\]
Thus every heterogeneous member has a unique target-pre coefficient, but the
definition imposes no common positive lower bound on its scalar pre-period Gram
\(\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}^2\).  All rank labels in this definition refer to the
separately normalized contrast indicator \(e_Q\), not to the fixed-rank law symbol
\(\mathfrak P_r\).

definitions.name: Donor-visible known-rank-two weak-pre-Gram class
definitions.construction:
For each sample-size triple, define
\[
 \mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}(N_0,K_T,K_D)
 =\left\{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D):
 e_Q=1,\ 
 \left[\int_{\mathcal I}\{b_{0,Q}(t)^2+b_{1,Q}(t)^2\}\,dt\right]^{1/2}
 \ge \frac12|a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_2\right\}.
\]
Here \(e_Q\), \(b_{0,Q}\), and \(b_{1,Q}\) are the separately normalized contrast indicator and factor curves in \(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}at\mbox{-}most\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}closure}\).  Thus this is a law class, not the image of a particular witness: every member has known contrast indicator one and donor-visible invariant joint contrast energy, while no common positive lower bound is imposed on \(\int_{\mathcal I}b_{0,Q}^2\).

definitions.name: Normalization-preserving weak-pre-Gram rank-two pair
definitions.construction:
For \(N_0\ge3\), put
\[
 \widetilde z_m=
 \frac{m-(N_0+1)/2}{\sqrt{(N_0^2-1)/12}},
 \qquad m\in\mathcal D,
 \qquad
 \bar h=\frac12\min\{h_\circ,R_1,M_\star\}>0,
 \qquad c_T=K_T^{-1},
\]
where \(R_1\) and \(M_\star\) are the fixed constants in \(\mathrm{ass:explicit\mbox{-}witness\mbox{-}compatibility}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:target\mbox{-}loading\mbox{-}bound}\).  Define raw factors
\[
 \widetilde b_{0,T}(t)=c_Ta_{\circ,0}\psi_\circ(t),
 \qquad
 \widetilde b_{1,T}(t)=a_{\circ,1}\psi_\circ(t).
\]
Let \(\varsigma_T\in\{-1,+1\}\) be the sign which makes the first nonzero value in the fixed countable dense sequence of probes from \(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}at\mbox{-}most\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}closure}\), applied to \((\varsigma_T\widetilde b_{0,T},\varsigma_T\widetilde b_{1,T})\), positive.  Set
\[
 s_{p,T}(t)=e^{-\lambda_\circ t},
 \qquad b_{p,T}=\varsigma_T\widetilde b_{p,T},
 \qquad z_m=\varsigma_T\widetilde z_m,
 \qquad z_\star^{(u)}=\varsigma_Tu\bar h,
 \qquad u\in\{-1,+1\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal I\), put
\[
 S_{p,m}^{(u)}(t)=s_{p,T}(t)+b_{p,T}(t)z_m,
 \qquad
 S_{p,\star}^{(u)}(t)=s_{p,T}(t)+b_{p,T}(t)z_\star^{(u)}.
\]
Continue every survival curve after \(\bar\tau\) by its value at \(\bar\tau\) times \(e^{-\lambda_\circ(t-\bar\tau)}\), set all censoring times equal to infinity, and sample all observed patients independently with the cell sizes \(K_{p,m}\).  Denote the induced laws by \(Q_{2,u}^{\mathrm{wk}}\), and set
\[
 \mathbb W_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)
 =(Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}}).
\]
This construction only names the laws.  Survival validity, class membership, exact rank, donor visibility, donor-span inclusion, target separation, and likelihood distance are properties to be proved.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), the canonical contrast dimension is \(d=0\), so \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)\) for every unit and \(\theta(t)=s_1(t)\). Along every regular submodel whose target-pre marginal law is fixed and which perturbs \(\theta\) through the post-control law, the score contribution of the target-pre records is identically zero. For fixed \(r\ge2\), any normalization-preserving loading path \(z_{\star,\eta}=z_\star+\eta v\) that remains in \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) has target derivative \(\left.\partial_\eta\theta_\eta(t)\right|_{\eta=0}=b_1(t)^\top v\), which is nonzero exactly when \(b_1^\top v\not\equiv0\) on \(\mathcal I\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)\).  Since \(d=r-1\), exact rank one gives \(d=0\).  Equivalently, \(\mathcal C_D\) has rank zero by \(\mathrm{ass:exact\mbox{-}centered\mbox{-}rank}\).  Under the zero-dimensional convention in \(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}factorization}\), the inner product \(b_p(t)^\top z_m\) is an empty sum and hence is zero.  Substitution into \(\mathrm{ass:normalized\mbox{-}factor\mbox{-}model}\) gives, for every \(p,m,t\),
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m=s_p(t).
\]
The target definition then yields
\[
 \theta(t)=S^0_{1,\star}(t)=s_1(t).
\]

Let \(\{P_\eta:|\eta|<\eta_0\}\) be a regular submodel covered by the claim, and write \(q_{0,\star,\eta}\) for the density of one target-pre record with respect to a common dominating measure.  The target-pre marginal is fixed along this path, so \(q_{0,\star,\eta}=q_{0,\star,0}\).  Its score is therefore
\[
 \left.\partial_\eta\log q_{0,\star,\eta}(O_{0,\star,j})\right|_{\eta=0}=0.
\]
Patient independence makes the target-pre sample score the sum of these zero contributions.  This proves the stated ancillarity for precisely the paths quantified in the corrected claim.

Finally fix \(r\ge2\) and a loading path \(z_{\star,\eta}=z_\star+\eta v\) that remains in the model.  The donor loadings and factor curves are fixed, so the primitive donor operator, its rank, and its singular values are fixed.  Endpoint normalization is preserved because \(b_1(0)=0\) in the canonical factorization.  Differentiating the target formula gives
\[
 \left.\partial_\eta\theta_\eta(t)\right|_{\eta=0}
 =\left.\partial_\eta\{s_1(t)+b_1(t)^\top(z_\star+\eta v)\}\right|_{\eta=0}
 =b_1(t)^\top v.
\]
This derivative is a nonzero element of \(C(\mathcal I)\) if and only if \(b_1^\top v\not\equiv0\). \(\square\)
statements.justification: The zero-dimensional collapse and the conditional loading derivative isolate the algebraic source of the rank discontinuity.
statements.gap: HanShah2025SSC imposes exact rank but does not separate normalization or state this score degeneracy.
statements.consumer: The result tells analysts exactly which target-pre paths are ancillary at rank one.

statements.statement:
Put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and center the functional-PCR map at the interpolated population panel \(\widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0\) defined in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and all sequences with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\to\infty\), there are independent mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes \(\phi_{T,j}\) and \(\phi_{D,p,m,j}\), a deterministic grid function \(\mathfrak b_r\), and a remainder \(Q_r\) such that, simultaneously for \(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)=Z_r(g)+\mathfrak b_r(g)+Q_r(g),
 \qquad
 Z_r=\mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}
     +n_D^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j},
\]
where \(\phi_{T,j}\equiv0\) when \(r=1\) and
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le \mathbf 1\{r\ge2\}\eta_D(K_D).
\]
The interpolated population comparison equals \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta\), and hence equals \(\theta\) at every grid point. For every sufficiently large evaluated triple, the finite-tail buffer and the conditional multiplier critical value in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\) obey
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}P\{\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>\omega_r/2\}
 \le\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)/4,
\]
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}P\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}>c_r^\xi+\omega_r/2\}
 \le\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)/4.
\]
Moreover \(\omega_r=o(\rho_r)\) uniformly on every three-dimensional tail without a restriction on the relative growth of \(K_T\) and \(N_0K_D\). The expansion and both tail inequalities are gridwise; the interpolation perturbation inside the \(L^2\) factor map is used to establish spectrum and Gram stability, while the discrepancy between \(S^0\) and \(\widetilde S^0\) away from the grid is carried only by \(c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}\) in the continuous-time band.
statements.justification: The expansion composes product-limit martingales with a stable interpolated-population functional-PCR map and exposes the two independent uncertainty channels.
statements.gap: Existing survival multiplier and PCR perturbation results do not jointly control interpolation inside the censored counterfactual factor operator, its deterministic risk-exhaustion bias, and finite-tail quantile transfer.
statements.consumer: It supplies the feasible gridwise approximation and explicit buffers needed for honest continuous-time inference.

statements.statement: For all sufficiently large \(N_0\ge2\), \(K_T\), and \(K_D\), the two laws in \(\mathrm{def:rank-two-lecam-pair}\) belong to \(\mathfrak P_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), have \(S_{p,m}^{(u)}(0)=1\), and differ in observed law only through the \(K_T\) target-pre failure times. Their target curves obey \(\|\theta_+-\theta_-\|_\infty=2|a_{\circ,1}|h_\circ\|\psi_\circ\|_\infty K_T^{-1/2}\). Their likelihood divergence satisfies \[D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_+\|P_-)\le K_T\int\frac{(f_{0,\star}^{(+)}-f_{0,\star}^{(-)})^2}{f_{0,\star}^{(-)}}\,dt\le\frac{4a_{\circ,0}^2h_\circ^2}{c_f}\int_0^{\bar\tau}\{\psi_\circ'(t)\}^2dt.\] A fixed sufficiently small \(h_\circ\) therefore yields uniformly bounded total variation while preserving exact total rank two, the donor contrast-spectrum bounds, the pre-contrast Gram bounds, and endpoint normalization.
statements.justification: The worked pair audits survival validity, exact rank, separation, and likelihood distance.
statements.gap: CattaneoFengTitiunik2021 has no normalization-preserving censored functional subexperiment.
statements.consumer: The pair supplies the target-pre channel in the minimax converse.

statements.statement:
There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)<\infty\) such that, for the piecewise-linear interpolant \(\widehat\theta_r\) in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr-multiplier-band}\),
\[
 0\le \|\widehat\theta_r-\theta\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}
 -\max_{g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}}|\widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)|
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{\min\{\beta+1,2\}}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\). Consequently the interpolation allowance under the corrected grid definition is \(O(\rho_r)\), so continuous-time honesty is not obtained by replacing \(\mathcal I\) with a fixed finite grid.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and set \(q=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\).  By the hazard identity and endpoint normalization,
\[
 \theta(t)=S^0_{1,\star}(t)
 =\exp\left\{-\int_0^t\lambda^0_{1,\star}(u)\,du\right\}.
\]
The bound \(\|\lambda^0_{1,\star}\|_{C^\beta(\mathcal I)}\le L\), the fixed horizon, and the product Hölder inequality applied to \(\theta'=-\lambda^0_{1,\star}\theta\) imply
\[
 \|\theta\|_{C^{\beta+1}(\mathcal I)}\le C(L,\bar\tau,\beta).
\]
Let \(I_{\mathcal G}\theta\) be the piecewise-linear interpolant of the grid values of \(\theta\).  On a grid interval \([a,b]\) of length at most \(h=h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), the first-order Taylor formula with Hölder remainder when \(q<2\), and the ordinary second-order interpolation remainder when \(q=2\), give
\[
 \sup_{t\in[a,b]}|I_{\mathcal G}\theta(t)-\theta(t)|
 \le C(L,\bar\tau,\beta)|b-a|^q.
\]
Taking the maximum over intervals yields
\[
 \|I_{\mathcal G}\theta-\theta\|_\infty\le c_{\mathrm{int}}h^q.
\]

By construction, \(\widehat\theta_r\) is linear between adjacent grid points.  Hence \(\widehat\theta_r-I_{\mathcal G}\theta\) is also linear there, and the maximum of its absolute value is attained at an endpoint.  Consequently
\[
 \|\widehat\theta_r-\theta\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}
 \le \max_{g\in\mathcal G}|\widehat\theta_r(g)-\theta(g)|
 +\|I_{\mathcal G}\theta-\theta\|_\infty.
\]
The reverse inequality between the grid maximum and the continuous supremum follows from \(\mathcal G\subset\mathcal I\).  Combining the last two displays proves the asserted two-sided interpolation inequality.  Finally, the corrected mesh condition is \(h^q\le\rho_r\), so the allowance is \(O(\rho_r)\). \(\square\)
statements.justification: The corrected exponent prices continuous-time interpolation at exactly the order supported by hazard smoothness and a linear interpolant.
statements.gap: HanShah2025SSC uses a finite evaluation grid and does not charge interpolation error to simultaneous coverage.
statements.consumer: It supports whole-trajectory clinical reporting once the stochastic band theorem is available.

statements.statement:
For each fixed \(r\ge1\), there is \(a_0<\infty\) such that, at every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), the band \(\widehat B_r\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\). There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\), independent of \(N_0\), \(K_T\), and \(K_D\), such that at every such triple,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)}E_P[w(\widehat B_r)]
 \le c_{\mathrm{up}}\bar\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).
\]
Both assertions hold uniformly over every three-dimensional tail, with no balanced-growth or relative-rate restriction. In particular, \(\bar\rho_1=\rho_1=(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\); for fixed \(r\ge2\), the displayed upper bound is \(O(\rho_r)\) on every subregime satisfying \(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r)\). No unrestricted higher-rank \(O(\rho_r)\) claim is made by this theorem.
statements.justification: This is the implementable honest patient-level replacement for the empirical donor bootstrap, with its exact estimator-specific width envelope.
statements.gap: HanShah2025SSC supplies finite-grid consistency and donor resampling, but not an interpolation-stable patient-martingale band with finite-tail coverage and a quantified total-estimator bias allowance.
statements.consumer: The PETAL Synthetic Survival Control analysis can report a valid simultaneous post-control survival band and its honest width guarantee.

statements.statement: There are constants \(a_0<\infty\) and \(c_{\mathrm{low}}>0\) such that, at every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), every \(B\in\mathcal H_1(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\) satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_1(N_0,K_T,K_D)}E_P[w(B)]\ge c_{\mathrm{low}}(N_0K_D)^{-1/2},\] and, for every fixed \(r\ge2\), every \(B\in\mathcal H_r(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\) satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)}E_P[w(B)]\ge c_{\mathrm{low}}\{K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\}.\] The donor channel uses a normalization-preserving post-donor hazard pair of size \((N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\). The target channel embeds the explicit rank-two pair from \(\mathrm{lem:rank-two-pair}\) and adds fixed orthogonal contrast directions for \(r>2\). All pairs preserve valid survival laws, endpoint normalization, exact primitive rank, the nonzero contrast-spectrum and pre-contrast Gram bounds, and uniformly bounded total variation.
statements.justification: The two explicit normalization-preserving pairs certify the unavoidable donor and target-pre channels.
statements.gap: Existing scalar synthetic-control decompositions do not supply these exact-rank survival-law converses.
statements.consumer: The lower bound prevents reporting a donor-only band when loading uncertainty is unavoidable.

statements.statement:
For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and every fixed exact rank \(r\), there are \(a_0<\infty\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, uniformly over every evaluated triple with \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\), without relative-growth restrictions,
\[
 W_1^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp(N_0K_D)^{-1/2},
\]
and, for \(r\ge2\),
\[
 c\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)
 \le W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 \le C\bar\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).
\]
Consequently \(W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) on every subregime satisfying \(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D))\).  Without that subregime condition, the displayed bracket is the proved unrestricted conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.  Each infimum is over bands satisfying the coverage constraint at that same evaluated triple.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(r\) and a sufficiently large evaluated triple.  By
\(\mathrm{thm:normalization\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}converse}\), every
admissible band has maximal expected width at least \(c\rho_r\).  Taking
the infimum over the same per-triple honesty class in
\(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}width}\) gives
\[
 W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\ge c\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).         \tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{thm:attaining\mbox{-}band}\), the explicit band
\(\widehat B_r\) is in that honesty class and obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}E_Pw(\widehat B_r)
 \le C\bar\rho_r.                                           \tag{2}
\]
Using \(\widehat B_r\) as a single data-dependent witness in the minimax
infimum yields
\[
 W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\le C\bar\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).     \tag{3}
\]
At rank one,
\(\bar\rho_1=\rho_1=(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\), so (1)--(3) prove
\[
 W_1^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)\asymp(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}.            \tag{4}
\]
For fixed \(r\ge2\), (1)--(3) give the unrestricted bracket
\[
 c\{K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\}
 \le W_r^*(N_0,K_T,K_D;\alpha)
 \le C\{K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}+\eta_D(K_D)\}.           \tag{5}
\]
Whenever \(\eta_D(K_D)=O(\rho_r)\), the two sides of (5) match and hence
\(W_r^*\asymp\rho_r\).  The constants and the common lower-tail cutoff are
uniform over every three-dimensional tail because the two input theorems
have that property.  No comparison among the relative growth rates has
been introduced.  The infimum on each line is the per-triple infimum from
\(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}width}\). \(\square\)
statements.justification: This is the exact rank-normalization transition at rank one and the honest unrestricted higher-rank minimax bracket delivered by the current total estimator and converse.
statements.gap: No located synthetic-control, survival-band, or low-rank inference paper gives the donor-only rank-one frontier or this explicit two-channel higher-rank bracket with its risk-exhaustion term.
statements.consumer: It tells trial and registry designers when the two-channel rate is matched and displays the precise residual width term outside that subregime.

statements.statement: On the homogeneous normalized special case \(r=1\), \(\widehat\theta_1\) and \(\widehat B_1\) reduce, up to the stated interpolation allowance, to the pooled donor-post Kaplan--Meier estimator and its patient-level martingale-multiplier simultaneous band based on \(N_0K_D\) observations.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check against classical one-sample survival-band theory.
statements.gap: DoblerPaulyScheike2019 validates martingale bands for survival functionals but does not derive this normalized Synthetic Survival Control reduction.
statements.consumer: It supplies a transparent implementation check for the rank-one software path.

statements.statement: In the general adaptation problem \(\mathcal A_0\subset\mathcal A\) with loss \(D\), Carpentier, Klopp, L\"offler, and Nickl define the minimax testing radius \(\rho_n\) by uniformly consistent tests of \(\mathcal A_0\) against \(\{f\in\mathcal A:D(f,\mathcal A_0)\ge L\rho_n\}\).  Their Theorem~2.1 states that if \(r_n(\mathcal A_0)=o(\rho_n)\), honest adaptation is impossible and every honest confidence set has expected \(D\)-diameter at least a constant multiple of \(\rho_n\) somewhere on \(\mathcal A_0\), under the displayed error-level restriction.

source.verbatim_statement: Let ρₙ be the minimax rate of testing for the testing problem and suppose that β₀ > 0 is as in the testing lower bound. Suppose that rₙ(A₀) = o(ρₙ). Then a honest and adaptive confidence set Cₙ for any α, α′ > 0 such that 0 < 2α + α′ < β₀ does not exist. In fact if 3α < β₀, then for any honest confidence set Cₙ we have sup_{f ∈ A₀} E_f |Cₙ|_D ≥ cρₙ for a constant c=c(α)>0.

upstream.citation: Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, Proposition 8.3.6; Alexandra Carpentier and Richard Nickl, On signal detection and confidence sets for low rank inference problems, proof of Theorem 4

attestation.note: Verified against the author-deposited arXiv source for arXiv:1608.04861 (source TeX lines 310--331), matching the published Definition 2.2 and Theorem 2.1. The source itself credits the stated antecedents recorded in --upstream.

statements.statement: Carpentier, Klopp, L\"offler, and Nickl, Theorem~2.2 and Section~7.1, construct an honest adaptive confidence set when a uniformly consistent composite test has separation no larger than the small-model estimation rate and an estimator satisfies their two-model oracle inequality.  The construction centers at the oracle estimator and chooses the radius \(r_n(\mathcal A)\Psi_n+r_n(\mathcal A_0)(1-\Psi_n)\); its coverage proof separately treats the null, alternatives far from the null, and alternatives within the testing radius.

source.verbatim_statement: Let α, α′ > 0 be given. Let ρₙ be the minimax rate of testing such that a min(α/2, α′)-uniformly consistent test exists. Assume that ρₙ ≤ C′rₙ(A₀). Moreover, assume that an oracle estimator f̂ at level α/2 exists. Then there exists a confidence set Cₙ that adapts to A₀ at level α′ and is honest at level α. Define Cₙ := {f ∈ A : D(f̂,f) ≤ K(rₙ(A)Ψₙ + rₙ(A₀)(1−Ψₙ))}. For coverage we investigate three distinct cases.

statements.statement:
Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent mean-zero random vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\) with finite third Euclidean moments, and let \(Y_i\) be independent centered Gaussian vectors with \(E(Y_iY_i^\top)=E(X_iX_i^\top)\). For every \(a>0\), there is a coupling of \(\sum_iX_i\) and \(\sum_iY_i\) such that, with \(B=a^{-3}\sum_iE\|X_i\|_2^3\),
\[
 \Pr\left\{\left\|\sum_iX_i-\sum_iY_i\right\|_2>3a\right\}
 \le C B\{1+|\log B|\},
\]
where \(C<\infty\) is universal. No nonsingularity or coordinate-variance lower bound is required.

statements.statement:
Let \(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\), let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be piecewise-linear interpolation on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and define \(\widetilde S^0\), \(\widetilde s\), \(\widetilde Y_m\), and \(\widetilde\Gamma\) as in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Put \(Y_m=(S^0_{0,m}-s_0,S^0_{1,m}-s_1)\) and \(\Gamma=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}Y_m\otimes Y_m\). There is a constant \(C_*<\infty\), depending only on the fixed model constants and \(r\), such that
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}(g)=S^0_{p,m}(g)\quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}),
 \qquad
 \max_{p,m}\|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_\infty
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
When \(d>0\), for every sufficiently fine grid the operator \(\widetilde\Gamma\) has exactly \(d\) positive eigenvalues, its \(d\)-th eigenvalue is at least \(\gamma_-^2/2\), and its selected projector \(\widetilde\Pi\) satisfies
\[
 \|\widetilde\Pi-\Pi\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
If \(\widetilde b_p\) denotes any selected positive-square-root factor coordinates of \(\widetilde\Gamma\), there is an orthogonal matrix \(R_{\mathcal G}\) such that
\[
 \max_{p\in\{0,1\}}\|\widetilde b_p-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}b_p\|_{L^2}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
Consequently, with \(H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}b_0b_0^\top\) and \(\widetilde H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}\widetilde b_0\widetilde b_0^\top\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widetilde H_0)\ge\kappa_-/2,
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde H_0^{-1}-R_{\mathcal G}^{\top}H_0^{-1}R_{\mathcal G}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_*h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta}.
\]
The population comparison curve is exact for the interpolated panel:
\[
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\theta
 \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal I,
 \qquad
 \theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{r,\mathcal G}(g)=\theta(g)
 \quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D});
\]
and for \(d=0\), the factor, projector, and Gram assertions use the zero-dimensional convention and the last display holds with \(\theta^{\mathrm{pop}}_{1,\mathcal G}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}s_1\).
statements.justification: This lemma closes the internal interpolation gap by stabilizing the population factor map before differentiation.
statements.gap: The existing grid proposition controls only output interpolation; it does not control the covariance operator and pre-period inverse computed from interpolated curves.
statements.consumer: The gridwise functional-PCR expansion is centered at this stable interpolated population map.

statements.statement:
For an observed control cell with \(k\) patients and \(k\) large enough, let \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\) be the deterministic piecewise-linear interpolation operator on \(\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}\), and set \(\widetilde S^0_{p,m}=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0_{p,m}\).  Its linearly interpolated Kaplan--Meier curve admits the uniform decomposition
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{p,m}-\widetilde S^0_{p,m}
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\varphi_{p,m,j}+b_{p,m,k}+q_{p,m,k}
 \quad\hbox{in }\ell^\infty(\mathcal I),
\]
where the \(\varphi_{p,m,j}\) are independent, mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes, \(\|b_{p,m,k}\|_\infty\le C_0e^{-c_0k}\), \(E q_{p,m,k}=0\), and \(E\|q_{p,m,k}\|_\infty^2\le C_0k^{-2}\), uniformly over the model class.  Here \(c_0=s_-g_-/3\), and \(C_0\) may be chosen as the conservative fixed constant used in the definition of \(\eta_D\).  Moreover, with \(q_\beta=\min\{\beta+1,2\}\),
\[
 \widetilde S^0_{p,m}(g)=S^0_{p,m}(g)\quad(g\in\mathcal G_{N_0,K_T,K_D}),
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_\infty
 \le c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
and
\[
 \|\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\|_{L^2(\mathcal I)}
 \le \bar\tau^{1/2}c_{\mathrm{int}}h_{N_0,K_T,K_D}^{q_\beta},
\]
where \(c_{\mathrm{int}}=c_{\mathrm{int}}(L,\bar\tau,\beta)<\infty\).  Thus the exact expansion about \(S^0_{p,m}\) contains the additional deterministic term \(a_{\mathcal G,p,m}=\widetilde S^0_{p,m}-S^0_{p,m}\), which is zero on the grid and is controlled only by the displayed interpolation bounds.  For independent donor cells, averaging the \(q_{p,m,k}\) terms has order \(O_P(N_0^{-1/2}k^{-1})=o_P((N_0k)^{-1/2})\), whereas averaging the bias or interpolation terms need not improve their respective uniform bounds.

Suppose an affine survival panel satisfies
\[
 S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)^\top z_m,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_m=0,
 \qquad
 N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}z_mz_m^\top=I_d,
 \qquad d=r-1.
\]
Set \(u_p^{\mathrm{HS}}(t)=(s_p(t),b_p(t)^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^r\) and \(v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}=(1,z_m^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^r\).  Then \(S^0_{p,m}(t)=\langle u_p^{\mathrm{HS}}(t),v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}\rangle\), the donor loading matrix \(V_D=[v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D]\) has full row rank \(r\), and \(v_\star^{\mathrm{HS}}\in\operatorname{span}\{v_m^{\mathrm{HS}}:m\in\mathcal D\}\).  In particular, every \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) is a specialized subclass member of the Han--Shah Theorem~1 survival factor model with donor-span inclusion; this implication does not assert that Han and Shah impose the canonical normalization, exact centered rank, spectrum, pre-Gram, smoothness, or loading-envelope restrictions defining \(\mathfrak P_r\).
statements.justification: This algebraic certificate locates the note's canonically normalized class as a strict specialization of the published Theorem~1 structural model without attributing the note's quantitative restrictions to Han and Shah.
statements.gap: HanShah2025SSC states generic factorization and donor-span inclusion but does not use the centered donor normalization or exact contrast-rank parameterization proved here.
statements.consumer: It licenses upward transfer of lower bounds by subclass inclusion while blocking any converse claim that the published class inherits this note's functional-PCR upper theorem.

statements.statement: Han and Shah's Theorem~1 structural model requires a finite-dimensional survival factorization \(S^{(0)}_{p,m}(t)=\langle u_p(t),v_m\rangle\) and, separately, inclusion of each treated-unit factor \(v_\star\) in the linear span of the donor factors.  The well-conditioned finite-grid pre-period matrix and latent time-period span restrictions are introduced later as Assumptions~7 and~8 for their Theorem~2, not as conditions of their Theorem~1.

source.locator: Assumptions 4 and 6 and Theorem 1 in Section 3.4.1; Assumption 7 in Section 3.4.3
source.verbatim_statement: Assumption 4 (Survival Factor Model). For all \(p\in[P]\), \(n\in[N]\) and \(t\in[0,\widetilde{\tau}]\), the potential survival function under control \(S^{(0)}_{p,n}(t)=\langle u_p(t),v_n\rangle\), where \(u_p:[0,\widetilde{\tau}]\to\mathbb R^r\) are (latent) period factors and \(v_n\in\mathbb R^r\) are (latent) unit factors for some \(r\ge1\). Assumption 6 (Linear Span Inclusion). For each treated unit \(n\in\mathcal I^{(1)}\), there exists weights \(w_{n,m}\in\mathbb R^{|\mathcal I^{(0)}|}\) such that \(v_n=\sum_{m\in\mathcal I^{(0)}}w_{n,m}\cdot v_m\). Theorem 1. Given the assumptions above, we have \(S^{(0)}_{1,n}(\cdot)=\sum_{m\in\mathcal I^{(0)}}w_{n,m}S^0_{1,m}(\cdot)\). Assumption 7 (Well-conditioned Spectrum). The expectation of the control group pre-treatment matrix satisfies: \(\operatorname{cond}(\mathcal S_{0,\mathcal I^{(0)}})\le\xi'\), and \(\|\mathcal S_{0,\mathcal I^{(0)}}\|_F^2\ge\xi''N_0T_0\) for some constants \(\xi',\xi''>0\), where \(\|\cdot\|_F\) is the Frobenius norm. Assumption 8 (Latent time-period span). We assume the post-period specific factors lie in the span of pre-period specific factors, i.e., \(\forall t\in\mathcal T,u_1(t)\in\operatorname{span}(\{u_0(s):s\in\mathcal T\})\) conditional on \(\{\mathcal{LF},\mathcal D\}\).

statements.statement:
Let \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), and let \((\bar b_p,\bar z_m)\) be any donor-centered compatible \(d\)-coordinate representation of the normalized factor model. After covariance normalization of its donor loadings, the donor-SVD factors and loadings in \(\mathrm{def:canonical\mbox{-}factorization}\) equal the compatible factors and loadings up to a common orthogonal transform. If \(d>0\), then \(S^0_{0,\star}-s_0\) belongs to the span of the canonical \(b_0\), the matrix \(H_0=\int_{\mathcal I}b_0b_0^\top\) is positive definite, and
\[
 z_\star=H_0^{-1}\int_{\mathcal I}b_0(t)
 \{S^0_{0,\star}(t)-s_0(t)\}\,dt
\]
is the unique compatible target coordinate. For \(d=0\), compatibility forces \(S^0_{p,m}=s_p\) for all units.
statements.justification: This supplies the missing algebra from target-pre factor compatibility to the unique canonical target loading.
statements.gap: A donor-operator SVD alone does not establish target span inclusion; the lemma uses the model's compatible all-unit factorization and the positive pre-period Gram.
statements.consumer: It validates the causal target coordinate used by functional PCR and the Han--Shah structural embedding.

statements.statement:
Let \(\theta_Q(t)=S^0_{1,\star}(t)\) for \(Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}(N_0,K_T,K_D)\).  There are constants \(a_0<\infty\) and \(c_\star>0\), independent of \(N_0,K_T,K_D\), such that, whenever \(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\ge a_0\),
\[
 c_\star\le
 \inf_{B:\ \inf_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}}
 Q\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\le\theta_Q(t)\le B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)
 \text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\}
 \ge1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)}
 \ \sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}}E_Q\{w(B)\}
 \le1.
\]
Hence the minimax expected supremum width over the donor-visible known-rank-two class has sharp order one.  Every member of this class has normalized contrast indicator one, full-row-rank donor loadings, and target loading in the donor span; in the fixed-design experiment it is therefore inside the factorization-and-span model used by Han--Shah Theorem~1.

The weak-pre-Gram pair \(\mathbb W_2(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) in \(\mathrm{def:weak\mbox{-}pre\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}pair}\) satisfies
\[
 \{Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}}\}
 \subset\mathfrak Q_{2,\mathrm{vis}}(N_0,K_T,K_D),
 \qquad
 \sigma_T=\{K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2+a_{\circ,1}^2\}^{1/2}\|\psi_\circ\|_2,
 \qquad
 H_{0,T}=K_T^{-2}a_{\circ,0}^2\|\psi_\circ\|_2^2,
\]
so \(\sigma_T\ge|a_{\circ,1}|\|\psi_\circ\|_2>0\) while \(H_{0,T}\to0\).  Its target separation is a fixed positive constant and
\(\operatorname{TV}(Q_{2,+}^{\mathrm{wk}},Q_{2,-}^{\mathrm{wk}})=O(K_T^{-1/2})\).

For a finite pre-period grid \(\mathcal T=\{t_1,\ldots,t_{T_0}\}\), put \(a=(e^{-\lambda_\circ t_\ell})_\ell\) and \(q=(\psi_\circ(t_\ell))_\ell\).  If \(a\) and \(q\) are linearly independent, the pair's pre-period donor matrix has rank two and the ratio of its largest to smallest nonzero singular value is at least a fixed positive constant times \(K_T\), so Han--Shah Assumption~7 fails for all sufficiently large \(K_T\).  If \(q\ne0\) is collinear with \(a\), the pre-period latent-factor span is one-dimensional and Han--Shah Assumption~8 fails for all sufficiently large \(K_T\).  If \(q=0\) on the grid, Assumptions~7--8 may hold, but the grid observes none of the perturbation and Han--Shah Theorem~2 does not address the pair's nonzero continuous-time target separation between grid points.  Thus the lower bound does not contradict their Theorem~2, and the functional-PCR upper bound over \(\mathfrak P_2\) does not transfer to this larger weak-pre-Gram class.

Let \(\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) be the separately normalized
rank-at-most-two closure in
\(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}at\mbox{-}most\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}closure}\).  There are
constants \(a_0<\infty\) and \(c_\star>0\), independent of
\(N_0,K_T,K_D\), such that, whenever
\(\min\{N_0,K_T,K_D\}\geq a_0\), every random continuous-time band \(B\)
satisfying
\[
\inf_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)}
Q\left\{B^{\mathrm{lo}}(t)\leq\theta_Q(t)\leq B^{\mathrm{up}}(t)
\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal I\right\}
\geq1-\alpha-\varepsilon_{N_0,K_T,K_D}(\alpha)
\]
also satisfies
\[
\sup_{Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\leq2}(N_0,K_T,K_D)}E_Q\{w(B)\}\geq c_\star.
\]
The constant band with endpoints zero and one has width one and is honest, so the
corresponding minimax maximal expected width is between \(c_\star\) and \(1\).
Hence its sharp order is one.  In particular, over the no-common-pre-Gram closure
there is no single rank-selection band attaining the vanishing known-rank oracle
widths \(\rho_1\) and \(\rho_2\).  This remains true on a rank-two subfamily whose
joint donor contrast singular value is bounded away from zero: donor-rank
detectability alone does not make the target loading estimable.
statements.justification: Uniform rank selection without a common pre-period strength bound must confront weak identification of the target loading even when donor rank is plainly detectable.
statements.gap: CarpentierKloppLofflerNickl2018 gives a general testing reduction for matrix-completion confidence sets, but not this normalization-preserving censored-survival obstruction with fixed target separation.
statements.consumer: It tells practitioners that a donor singular-value rule cannot support shrinking honest SSC bands unless target-relevant pre-period strength is anchored or separated.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(r=1\), put \(n_D=N_0K_D\),
\[
 \bar G_D(t)=N_0^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}G_{1,m}(t),
 \qquad H_D(t)=s_1(t)\bar G_D(t).
\]
For the continuously interpolated pooled donor-post product-limit estimator in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\), there are independent mean-zero processes
\[
 \phi_{m,j}^{\mathrm{pool}}(t)
 =-s_1(t)\int_0^tH_D(u)^{-1}\,dM_{m,j}(u)
\]
such that, on the inference grid,
\[
 \widehat\theta_1-\theta
 =n_D^{-1}\sum_{m\in\mathcal D}\sum_{j=1}^{K_D}
 \mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\phi_{m,j}^{\mathrm{pool}}
 +b_{D,n_D}+q_{D,n_D},
\]
where
\[
 \|b_{D,n_D}\|_\infty\le Ce^{-cn_D},
 \qquad Eq_{D,n_D}=0,
 \qquad E\|q_{D,n_D}\|_\infty^2\le Cn_D^{-2},
\]
uniformly over the rank-one class although the censoring laws may differ across donors. If \(\widehat Z_1^\xi\) is the explicit pooled multiplier and \(\Sigma_1\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_1\) are respectively the covariance kernel of the first-order sum and the conditional covariance kernel of that multiplier, then
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_1}E_P
 \left\|n_D^{-1}\sum_{m,j}
 \mathcal L_{\mathcal G}\phi_{m,j}^{\mathrm{pool}}\right\|_
 {\infty,\mathcal I}^2
 +\sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_1}E_PE_\xi
 \|\widehat Z_1^\xi\|_{\infty,\mathcal I}^2
 \le Cn_D^{-1},
\]
and
\[
 n_D\|\widehat\Sigma_1-\Sigma_1\|_{\infty,\mathcal I^2}
 \longrightarrow0
\]
in probability uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_1\). These assertions allow variance-zero coordinates, including time zero. No random-quantile coverage assertion is made.
statements.justification: This is the missing pooled rank-one product-limit and patient-multiplier theorem under donor-specific censoring.
statements.gap: A one-cell Kaplan--Meier expansion does not justify pooling independent but non-identically censored donor cohorts.
statements.consumer: It closes the exact-rank-one attaining rate and supplies the implementation-level pooled multiplier.

statements.statement:
Fix \(r\ge1\), and let \(n_{\mathrm{eff},r}\), \(\delta_{r,n}(\alpha)\), \(\chi_{r,n}\), and \(\tau_{r,n}\) be the deterministic sequences in \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Let \(Z_r\) be the oracle patient linear process in \(\mathrm{lem:pooled\mbox{-}noniid\mbox{-}km\mbox{-}linearization}\) when \(r=1\) and in \(\mathrm{lem:stabilized\mbox{-}gridwise\mbox{-}fpcr\mbox{-}transfer}\) when \(r\ge2\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\) and every three-dimensional tail,
\[
 \chi_{r,n}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\tau_{r,n}}{\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)}=\chi_{r,n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
For every sufficiently large evaluated triple,
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}
 P\left\{\|Z_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}
 \le \widetilde c_r^\xi+\tau_{r,n}\right\}
 \ge 1-\alpha+\frac12\delta_{r,n}(\alpha)
 \ge1-\alpha-o(1),
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P_r}E_P\widetilde c_r^\xi
 \le C\rho_r(N_0,K_T,K_D).
\]
The result permits singular covariance matrices and zero-variance coordinates, including the coordinate at time zero; \(\widetilde c_r^\xi\) is the measurable left-continuous generalized-inverse conditional \(1-\alpha+\delta_{r,n}(\alpha)\) quantile.
statements.justification: This theorem validates the data-dependent functional-PCR multiplier quantile uniformly over the canonical grid without a coordinate-variance floor.
statements.gap: Classical multiplier results do not directly cover the estimated projector, square root, inverse pre-Gram, stabilized product-limit derivatives, fallback branches, and singular coordinates in one unrestricted-relative-growth theorem.
statements.consumer: It supplies the stochastic critical radius used by the honest continuous-time functional-PCR band.

statements.statement:
Fix \(r\ge2\), put \(n_D=N_0K_D\), and use the stabilized full-cell and odd--even half-fold inputs in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). Uniformly over \(\mathfrak P_r(N_0,K_T,K_D)\), the aggregate functional-PCR estimator has the gridwise expansion
\[
 \widehat\theta_r-\theta
 =K_T^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_T}\phi_{T,j}
 +n_D^{-1}\sum_{p,m,j}\phi_{D,p,m,j}
 +\mathfrak b_r+Q_r,
\]
where the patient processes are independent and mean zero,
\[
 \|\mathfrak b_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}\le\eta_D(K_D),
 \qquad E\|Q_r\|_{\infty,\mathcal G}^2\le C\upsilon_r^2,
\]
with \(\upsilon_r\) as in the corrected definition of \(\omega_r\). The aggregate spectral/pre-Gram threshold failure probability is at most \(Ce^{-cn_D}\), without a union over donor cells. On the regular branch, composition of the first two Fr\'echet derivatives of the coordinate-free prediction map with the stabilized inputs gives deterministic patient envelopes \(C/K_T\) for target-pre patients and \(C/(N_0K_D)\) for donor patients on every dataset. On fallback, the ordinary pooled derivative is used. Consequently, for the oracle linear process \(Z_r\) and the empirical multiplier process \(\widehat Z_r^\xi\),
\[
 \sup_PE_P\|Z_r\|_\infty^2
 +\sup_PE_PE_\xi\|\widehat Z_r^\xi\|_\infty^2
 \le C\{K_T^{-1}+n_D^{-1}\}=C\rho_r^2.
\]
All bounds are continuous-time bounds and incur no \(\sqrt{\log|\mathcal G|}\) factor.

Fix an observed control cell or deterministic half-fold containing \(k\) patients, put \(h_0=s_-g_-\), \(\ell_k=\max\{1,kh_0/8\}\), and let \(\widehat S_k^\dagger\) be the stabilized product-limit curve in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:fpcr\mbox{-}multiplier\mbox{-}band}\). For all sufficiently large \(k\): (i) \(\widehat S_k^\dagger\) equals the ordinary Kaplan--Meier curve on \(\{Y_k(\bar\tau)\ge\ell_k\}\); (ii)
\[
 P\{Y_k(\bar\tau)<kh_0/8\}
 \le \exp\{-49h_0k/128\}\le e^{-c_0k},
 \qquad c_0=h_0/3;
\]
(iii) changing one patient record changes the entire interpolated stabilized curve by at most \(C/k\), deterministically on every dataset; (iv) every individual observed multiplier contribution has supremum norm at most \(C/k\), deterministically; and (v), with \(\widetilde S^0=\mathcal L_{\mathcal G}S^0\), there are independent mean-zero censoring-martingale influence processes \(\varphi_{k,j}\), a deterministic bias \(b_k^\dagger\), and a centered remainder \(q_k^\dagger\) such that
\[
 \widehat S_k^\dagger-\widetilde S^0
 =k^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^k\varphi_{k,j}+b_k^\dagger+q_k^\dagger,
 \qquad
 \|b_k^\dagger\|_\infty\le Ce^{-c_0k},
 \qquad
 E\|q_k^\dagger\|_\infty^2\le Ck^{-2}.
\]
For independent donor cells, their centered rare-cell contributions average with second moment at most \(CN_0^{-1}e^{-c_0k}\le C(N_0k^2)^{-1}\). All assertions allow ties and all realized risk sets; no all-cells-good event is imposed.

sampling_model.design: Fixed two-period panel with one target unit observed under control only before intervention and \(N_0\) donor units observed under control in both periods.
sampling_model.units: Independent right-censored patient records within the target-pre cohort and every donor-period cohort.
sampling_model.treatment: The target receives treatment after the intervention; its missing post-control survival curve is the causal estimand, while donor exposure remains control.
sampling_model.overlap: Event and censoring survival probabilities are uniformly positive on \(\mathcal I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The primitive centered donor survival operator has exactly \(r-1\) bounded nonzero singular directions. Cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves feed the corresponding covariance-normalized functional-PCR map, and patient-level counting-process multipliers jointly re-estimate donor and target-pre uncertainty.

The observed-data functional is the guarded pair \((\widehat\theta_r,\widehat B_r)\). Its minimax guarantees are

tldr: The project studies the entire post-control survival trajectory for a treated unit in the exact-factor Synthetic Survival Control model. Exact total rank is imposed primitively through a centered donor survival operator with exactly \(r-1\) nonzero directions and bounded contrast spectrum, which makes the covariance-normalized factor coordinates and functional PCR well defined. At exact rank one there is no target loading to estimate, so the optimal per-triple honest band has donor-patient width \((N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\); at every fixed rank at least two, target-pre loading uncertainty survives and the sharp width is \(K_T^{-1/2}+(N_0K_D)^{-1/2}\). A censoring-aware functional-PCR band attains this frontier under a deterministic coverage-error schedule that vanishes on every three-dimensional tail, while explicit normalization-preserving survival-law pairs give the matching converse without relative-growth restrictions.

project_justification.gap: Han and Shah establish identification and finite-grid consistency for Synthetic Survival Control but do not provide uniformly honest continuous-time bands, patient-level propagation through PCR, or a minimax converse; their PETAL interval resamples donors only.
project_justification.niche: Normalization \(S(0)=1\) creates a rank-specific information geometry absent from scalar synthetic-control inference: a primitive zero-rank donor contrast operator has no heterogeneous target loading, whereas every positive fixed contrast rank can carry a target-pre channel.
project_justification.fill: The project derives canonical coordinates from an exact-rank, bounded-spectrum donor operator, defines minimax width over bands constrained at each evaluated sample triple, obtains an arbitrary-relative-growth functional expansion and attaining multiplier band, and supplies matching lower bounds including an explicit rank-two target-loading pair.

related_work: HanShah2025SSC supplies the causal survival-panel setup, exact factor restriction, Kaplan--Meier first stages, and PCR consistency that motivate the target, but it does not analyze per-triple uniform coverage or minimax expected width. AgarwalShahShen2025PCR supplies the minimum-norm and row-space PCR map and its strong-factor geometry; the present class makes that geometry primitive through exact centered-operator rank and bounded nonzero spectrum. DoblerPaulyScheike2019 supplies the patient counting-process multiplier construction for time-simultaneous survival inference. CattaneoFengTitiunik2021 supplies the conceptual separation between pre-fit and post-prediction uncertainty for scalar synthetic controls, while the explicit rank-two survival pair here isolates the target-loading channel and calculates its likelihood divergence. ImbensViviano2026 shows in a different random-factor model that valid synthetic-control inference depends on which stochastic channel remains after conditioning. GoldsmithGrevenCrainiceanu2013 accounts for decomposition uncertainty in functional principal-component bands but has neither censoring nor a causal missing curve. CarpentierKloppLofflerNickl2018 informs the open rank-adaptation question through its testing reduction. CurthPoonNoriGonzalez2024 and AtheyBayatiDoudchenkoImbensKhosravi2021 motivate, but are not theorem-level targets of, the separate approximate-rank extension.
technical_internal_limitation: The lower frontier is minimax over an exact-rank class. It does not claim that every individual rank-at-least-two law has a nonzero target-pre variance component; a particular law with a vanishing post contrast can be easier. Exact rank is also not an approximation-bias guarantee, so approximate-rank robustness remains a distinct proposal angle.
honest_scope: The closed claims concern known fixed total rank defined by a primitive centered donor operator, exactly \(r-1\) nonzero contrast directions with uniform lower and upper spectrum bounds, independent right censoring, a fixed follow-up horizon, smooth hazards, and patient sampling in the target-pre and donor cells. Honesty is imposed at every evaluated sample triple with a fixed deterministic coverage-error allowance that vanishes uniformly on three-dimensional tails. The exact rank-one reduction recovers the classical pooled donor-post survival band. Unknown-rank adaptation remains an open-ended composite-testing question, and covariate-dependent censoring is reserved for a separate efficiency problem.
